newsitem.title: CANADA: DBRS confirms, upgrades Petro-Canada debt.
newsitem.headline: DBRS confirms, upgrades Petro-Canada debt.

text.p: Dominion Bond Rating Service said on Thursday it confirmed its rating on Petro-Canada's commercial paper at R-1 (low) and upgraded its rating on the firm's unsecured notes and debentures to A.
The trend on all issues was rated as stable.

DBRS said the confirmation on commercial paper came as a result of Petro-Canada's debt-equity ratio remaining at stable levels and a positive outlook for operations in the context of currently strong oil and gas prices.

DBRS said it raised its rating on unsecured notes and debentures to A from A (low) because Petro-Canada has achieved meaningful savings in operating and overhead expenses and reduced its reliance on higher-cost production with its C$731 million acquisition of Amerada Hess Canada.

Earnings were expected to be impacted negatively with the amortization of non-tax-deductible goodwill from the acquisition, but DBRS said it expected that would decline in importance as projects such Hibernia come on stream.
It said Petro-Canada's debt levels increased moderately because of the Hess acquisition but were at acceptable levels.
